Native checks again on the socket queue, before and after reading, that the connection is still open and its approval live (ControlSocket.admits), drops any reply to a connection whose approval ran out (ControlSocket.reply), and checks the approval again before the writer starts each line (ControlConnection mayWrite), so a line queued behind a slow reader never starts after the approval ends. The token is read from the engine's dedicated ac_cli_devtools_endpoint call when the engine has it (callForSecretReply, bytes wiped), never from the shared ac_cli_control status, else from ArdiaControl.json opened O_NOFOLLOW, required a regular file of the user's with no group or other bits and no access list letting others in (PrivateFolder.privateFile), at most 64 KiB, whose port, generation and pid match the running server (DevtoolsEndpoint.read); it must be 16 to 256 base64url characters. Refused while control is off, at arrival and again after the read; turning control off cuts native off synchronously (ControlSocket.cutOff, one lock shared by the writer, replies, admission and the token read) before the asynchronous stop; where the socket has no doorbell (Linux, Windows) the method is unlisted and answers unknown_method. In JS it is a Secret of kind devtoolsToken from the moment it arrives (platform/automation.ts) and is revealed only on that one reply line (socketDevtools.devtoolsEndpointLine).
